expected_issues.description:
`OptionalEncryptableName` is used in this file (e.g., `pub merchant_name: OptionalEncryptableName`), but the import is now gated with `#[cfg(feature = "v1")]`. If that usage is not also strictly behind `cfg(feature = "v1")`, builds with `--features v2` will fail with an unresolved type/import.

Fix options:
- Widen the import gate to `#[cfg(any(feature = "v1", feature = "v2"))]` (or remove the cfg if harmless), or
- Ensure every usage of `OptionalEncryptableName` is behind the same `cfg(feature = "v1")` gate.

Given the type looks like a shared model type, widening the import is usually safest.

expected_issues.title: Feature flag inconsistency detected: The `PaymentMethodMigrationResponseType` type alias…
expected_issues.description:
Feature flag inconsistency detected: The `PaymentMethodMigrationResponseType` type alias and its `From` implementation are now conditionally compiled with `#[cfg(all(any(feature = "v2", feature = "v1"), not(feature = "payment_methods_v2")))]`, but the `PaymentMethodMigrationResponse` struct (line 2291) and `MigrationStatus` enum (line 2311) have no feature flags.

This creates a compilation issue because:
1. The struct and enum are always available
2. The `From` implementation is only available under specific feature combinations
3. Code in `crates/router/src/core/payment_methods/migration.rs` uses `PaymentMethodMigrationResponse::from(...)` without feature guards

Suggestion: Add the same feature flag guards to both `PaymentMethodMigrationResponse` struct and `MigrationStatus` enum to maintain consistency:
```rust
#[cfg(all(
    any(feature = "v2", feature = "v1"),
    not(feature = "payment_methods_v2")
))]
#[derive(Debug, Default, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct PaymentMethodMigrationResponse { ... }

#[cfg(all(
    any(feature = "v2", feature = "v1"),
    not(feature = "payment_methods_v2")
))]
#[derive(Debug, Default, serde::Serialize)]
pub enum MigrationStatus { ... }
```
